Sieve is the only AI research lab exclusively focused on video data.

Video already makes up 80% of internet traffic and has become the dominant medium driving creativity, communication, gaming, AR/VR, and robotics. Unlocking the ability to truly model video is the key to breakthroughs across all of these domains but progress has been bottlenecked by one thing: high-quality training data. That’s where Sieve comes in.

We bring together exabyte-scale video infrastructure, novel video understanding techniques, and dozens of diverse data sources to create datasets that push the frontier of video modeling. This unique combination allows us to deliver data with unmatched precision, quality, and speed which has earned the trust of frontier AI labs, Fortune 100 companies, and fast-growing generative AI startups.
long_description.after:
Sieve builds the data and environments frontier AI labs use to train the next generation of multimodal systems.

AI is moving beyond chatbots into video, audio, images, software, robotics, and interactive worlds. The next generation of models will need to understand how the world looks, sounds, moves, responds, and changes over time. Progress is bottlenecked by one thing: high-quality data.

long_description.before:
Datoric provides custom training data for voice models, robotics, and world models. We manage the full process from contributor recruitment and task design to secure collection, quality control, rights management, and delivery.

Our collection infrastructure is private by design. Voice, robotics, and world-model projects run through separate applications and sites, so contributor pools, task requirements, incentives, and data flows do not mix across modalities. Within each system, customer projects are isolated in private workspaces. Only approved contributors can access assigned tasks, with no public task listings, upload links, or contributor APIs.

We also build quality into the collection process instead of relying only on review after the data arrives. Contributors are qualified and matched before they participate, collection requirements are enforced inside each workflow, and early submissions are tested before a project scales. Every sample is then linked to its contributor, consent, usage rights, collection history, and review record.

Datoric’s mission is to make human-generated training data more secure, reliable, and responsibly sourced from the moment it is created.
long_description.after:
Datoric develops custom datasets for voice models, robotics, and world models, treating research, collection, verification, and production as one continuous process. We work closely with frontier model teams to turn emerging limitations into testable data hypotheses, while running our own experiments ahead of customer demand. This allows us to operationalize validated methods into repeatable collection systems at scale.

Data is collected through private invite-only applications separated by modality, customer, and trust level. Every submission remains linked to the contributor, device, task, session, consent, rights, and processing history that produced it, giving our internal QA and fraud models the context to detect problems that may appear legitimate in the finished file. Each collection reveals new failure cases and quality signals that improve the systems behind the next dataset.

Once a collection method is validated, it becomes a reusable data recipe for future custom projects or independently collected, rights-cleared data products. This allows Datoric to turn what is emerging at the frontier into datasets available ahead of broader market demand.

one_liner.before: Security-first training data
one_liner.after: Security-first training data your next model needs

long_description.before:
We build collaborative robot squads for solar farm construction.

High labor costs, labor shortages, and unpredictable productivity make infrastructure difficult to build in places that are remote, harsh, or empty. We are building robots to unlock places once considered too difficult to develop. Solar farm is our first proving ground.

Unlike solutions that automate only one task, or even part of one, we cover the workflow after PV module pallets arrive on-site: transportation, installation, alignment, and fastening. Each robot has a specific role, and fleets can be configured based on each project’s cost and schedule requirements.

Our robots operate autonomously with remote supervision. One person can supervise 4+ robots through a screen and an e-stop button, without being physically present or teleoperating them. Our robotic fleet has also been tested at night, paving the way for 24/7 operation.

We work directly with EPCs through a Robotics-as-a-Service model, requiring no robot purchase or large upfront capital investment. We also work with racking and PV module manufacturers to certify compatibility and give customers confidence in deployment.

Purpose-built hardware, multimodal sensing, and physical AI software help our robots handle real-world construction uncertainty.
long_description.after:
We’re building collaborative robotic crews for large-scale infrastructure projects, including solar farms and data centers.

002C: “002A, 5.3 mm left.”
002B: “002A, you’re running low. Next pallet is on the way.”
002C: “Am I clear to come in?”
002A: “Aligned. Panel released. You’re clear.”
002C: “Fastening.”
002B: “Next load arriving now.”

This isn’t a human crew talking. It’s three robots building a utility-scale solar farm together. 

Our AI control system enables specialized robots to collaborate, learn reusable construction skills, like alignment, fastening, and manipulation, and transfer them across workflows, from solar farms to data centers. 🚧 🦺

one_liner.after: Robotic crews for large-scale infrastructure construction

long_description.before:
Litmus gives back the hours your team burns on interviews, while holding every candidate to your technical bar. It builds assessments from your repos, tickets, and job descriptions, and candidates work through them in their own setup with the tools they actually use. Litmus runs and tests every submission, and grades outcome, process, and tool fluency, down to AI prompting.

Send assessments async to filter unqualified applicants before an engineer wastes an hour on a call. Or run them live, where Litmus tracks everything candidates say and build, so your engineers can focus on the person instead of taking notes, and the scorecard is written before they leave the call.

It's sent 3,000+ assessments on behalf of Neo Scholars, Mercor, Composio, and more.
long_description.after:
Litmus is building the most accurate framework for evaluating and benchmarking human capability, starting with software.

AI will compound small differences in human capability into increasingly large differences in what people can accomplish, while making existing static benchmarks obsolete. Software is already there: AI can hill-climb any output-based evaluation, while the ability to direct it is becoming the defining advantage. 

Litmus applies the same approach we already use for model evals to humans – creating world-like environments, and inspecting trajectory instead of just output.

Every knowledge industry will soon face the same problem. We build Litmus to tell you what humans are capable of.

We're already helping build frontier technical teams at Mercor, Composio, Neo Scholars, and more.

Alchemize is a code review platform that helps teams understand PRs and ship faster.

Agentic coding has 10x’d code output. Teams are opening larger PRs more frequently, but the current tools don’t support this new coding paradigm. 

Alchemize automatically breaks down PRs into guided, understandable reviews. It breaks each PR into manageable, smaller PRs that reveals the original author’s (human or agent) intent. We show where changes begin, how data flows, and which decisions require human judgment.
long_description.after:
Alchemize helps teams review and test code written by humans and coding agents.

Agentic coding has 10x’d code output. Teams are opening larger PRs more frequently, but existing review workflows have not kept up.

Alchemize breaks large changes into smaller, dependency-ordered PRs and guided reviews. It shows the prompts and intent behind agent-written code, then uses browser agents to test affected workflows. Reviewers can quickly understand how a change works, what the agent assumed, and where human judgment is needed. Teams ship faster with more confidence.

Every customer has different context, exceptions do not follow clean rules, and the next step is often buried in emails, portals, handoffs, or someone’s memory. Rex is the #1 winner of the Vercel AI Accelerator out of 2,500 teams, selected by Guillermo Rauch and leaders from OpenAI, Anthropic, Browserbase and more.

long_description.before:
Floracene lets any healthcare operator describe the internal tool they need and deploy it in one click - connected to production data, with read and write access scoped by the user. Think Lovable or Retool, except purpose-built for the needs of healthcare business that has no engineering team.

The bottleneck in healthcare isn't building anymore. Anyone can vibecode an 80% solution in an afternoon, custom to their own workflow, with people already on staff. The tool then dies locally on the builder’s computer, because IT (correctly) won't let anyone deploy a tool touching PHI without first-class authentication and permissioning. Our first design partner had multiple employees who had each built useful tools and dashboards locally, but couldn’t actually share these with coworkers or connect to their core practice data. Within weeks of implementing Floracene, they were able to cut a $12K / month contract for a crappy dashboarding tool and had 4 home-built tools shipped to production.

~$200B is spent on administrative software in healthcare every year in the US. Tens of thousands of those companies still run core operations on spreadsheets, and we're at the top of the first inning of AI adoption.

Asaph and Jonah met on the hospitals team at Palantir two years ago, and have each spent the last four years in the plumbing of US healthcare: claims, eligibility, and payor contracting. Asaph was an early PM at Garner. Jonah was a founding engineer at Metriport (YC S22) after starting his own fax-automation startup for fertility clinics.
